To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have solved the structure of a T3SS associated protein, CT584, from C. trachomatis at 3.05 Å resolution and that this structure is highly similar to the recently reported Cpn0803 structure.
CT584 is a hexamer composed of three dimers, which is highly homologous to the Cpn0803 structure, and the CT584 structure is the first reported structure from Chlamydiaceae family.
the structure of CT583 from Chlamydiatrachomatis has been refined to 3 Å resolution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the structure and function of CT584 and how its structure relates to other chlamydial T3SS-associated proteins.
understanding the structure and function of the T3SS and its associated proteins.
elucidating the molecular basis of chlamydial pathogenesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the structure of CT583 is highly similar to that of Cpn0803 and that both proteins form a trimer of homodimers.
CT584 is a hexamer composed of a trimer-of-dimers that is highly similar to Cpn0803.
CT584 is a hexamer with a dimeric subunit structure, and the structure of CT583 is similar to the Cpn0803 structure from C. pneumoniae.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the crystal structure of a Chlamydia T3SS-associated effector protein is reported and that the protein is a hexamer that shares high similarity to the Cpn0803 protein from Chlamydiapneumoniae.
the structure of the CT584 hexamer provides a framework for understanding the molecular mechanisms of T3SS protein secretion.
we have solved the structure of a T3SS protein from C. trachomatis, and that it is very similar to an orthologous structure from another Chlamydia species.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CT584 is a highly conserved protein that is likely to be involved in chlamydial T3SS assembly and/or function, which is important to the understanding of chlamydial pathogenesis.
the structure of CT585 is highly conserved across the Chlamydia species, and that this structure is likely to be a conserved feature of the T3SS apparatus across all Chlamydia spp.
CT584, like Cpn0803 in C. pneumoniae, is an essential T3SS protein, which is likely involved in the regulation of chlamydial T3SS activity.
